goal: New flywheel.audit module exposes a chronologically-merged stream(run_id, follow=...) iterator and an opt-in attach_logger emitter backed by the store's read_audit_since cursor.

references: src/flywheel/store_protocols.py -- AuditStore protocol's read_audit_since is the canonical read path; the library wraps it
src/flywheel/lifecycle.py -- Status.DONE / Status.FAILED / etc. terminal-status set; the follow loop checks lifecycle.status to decide when to stop polling
src/flywheel/store_memory.py -- defensive-copy discipline; any record yielded to a caller is detached from internal storage
constraints: Create src/flywheel/audit.py exposing: AuditRecord = EventRecord | SdkMessageRecord (re-exported from store_protocols); stream(run_id: str, *, store: AuditStore, follow: bool = False, poll_interval: float = 0.25) -> Iterator[AuditRecord]; attach_logger(logger: logging.Logger, *, run_id: str, store: AuditStore, poll_interval: float = 0.25) -> AuditLoggerHandle; AuditLoggerHandle with .detach() that stops emission and joins the background thread.
stream(follow=False): reads everything currently persisted via repeated read_audit_since(run_id, cursor) calls until the store returns an empty page, then returns. Cursor starts at 0.

stream(follow=True): same as above, then loops sleeping poll_interval seconds between read_audit_since calls. Terminates when the lifecycle reaches a terminal status (Status.DONE, Status.FAILED, Status.INTERNAL_ERROR, Status.INTERRUPTED, Status.BLOCKED) AND a subsequent read_audit_since returns no new records (drain-then-exit ordering avoids dropping the final write).
Unknown run_id: stream yields nothing and returns. No exception. (Spec error-handling table.)

attach_logger: spawns a daemon thread that subscribes to stream(run_id, follow=True) and emits each record as logger.log(logging.INFO, msg, extra={'audit_record': record_as_dict}) where msg is a short human-readable label like 'audit run=<id> seq=<n> kind=<k>'. Detaching joins the thread with a short timeout (1s). No global side effects; calling attach_logger twice with the same logger returns distinct handles.

flywheel.audit MAY import logging, threading, time, and stdlib utilities; it is not subject to the pure-module discipline that applies to flywheel.task / flywheel.lifecycle. Do not import claude_agent_sdk (the audit stream traffics in opaque dicts/dataclasses already produced upstream).
Re-export the public surface from flywheel.__init__ if and only if the package already re-exports peer modules (check first; do not introduce a new __init__ re-export pattern unilaterally).

tests/test_audit.py (new): cover (a) stream(follow=False) drains every persisted record in sequence order for a fixture run with mixed events + SDK messages; (b) stream(unknown_run_id) yields nothing; (c) stream(follow=True) running in a thread observes records written concurrently, and exits cleanly when the lifecycle transitions to Status.DONE; (d) attach_logger captures every persisted audit record exactly once via a custom logging.Handler that records calls; (e) detach() stops emission and joins the thread.
Use the InMemoryStore from tests/test_store_contract.py as the test substrate; do not require sqlite / postgres for the library suite.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not build the CLI in this task -- that is audit-cli.
Do not add filtering by kind/attempt/iteration -- spec lists those as explicit MVP non-goals.
Do not implement push notifications (LISTEN/NOTIFY, callbacks, asyncio queues). Polling-with-cursor is the chosen mechanism per the spec Decisions Log.
Do not change the store protocol -- this task consumes the API added in audit-schema-and-protocol.
edge_cases: Live follower polls during a write: read_audit_since is transactional (per the store contract); partial writes are invisible. The library trusts this and does not retry on its own.
Concurrent CLI followers: each call to stream() creates its own cursor; both observe the same total ordering.
Records with identical timestamps: sequence breaks the tie. The library does not re-sort -- it trusts read_audit_since to return in sequence order.
follow=True against an already-terminal run: drains once via read_audit_since, observes the terminal lifecycle status, returns without sleeping.
Logger handle: detach() during emission must not raise; the thread checks a stop flag between polls and finishes the current page before exiting.

graders.run: uv run python -c "from flywheel.audit import stream, attach_logger, AuditRecord; assert callable(stream) and callable(attach_logger)"
graders.name: public-surface
